name: Tersk
notes: The Tersk Stud in Stavropol Krai, founded 1921, rebuilding a Russian riding horse out of the last Strelets horses with Arabian, Don and Kabardin blood. Recognised as its own breed in 1948. Bigger and longer-lined than the Arabian it looks like.
Silvery grey is the whole visual identity and the pool is built for it: about seven founders in eight go grey, over a bay-leaning base, and the rest stay bay, chestnut or black.

It is grey and not silver, and the difference matters. Grey is progressive depigmentation over a pigmented foal coat; silver dilutes black pigment and comes with eye trouble. Silver is forced wild here, along with cream, pearl, champagne, mushroom, dun and flaxen - the same distinction the breed's own name for the colour keeps blurring.
Nothing white: every pinto locus, roan, rabicano and the leopard complex are forced wild. No source describes a patterned pure Tersk.
All disorders clear. Arabian foundation is not an Arabian carrier rate - the SCID, CA and LFS numbers that exist are Arabian samples, and a Tersk has Strelets, Don and Kabardin behind it as well.
Tolerant both ways and lightly: the taboon system leaves them out on North Caucasus range through hot summers and real winters, sorted by both rather than specialised for either.
The dry Arabian head, the high tail set, the fine skin and hair, and the taboon management itself are none of them modelled.
